transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
House Republicans have voted for a new leader for the next Congress.
Ohio Congressman Jim Jordan defeated the number two in House GOP leadership currently, Steve
Scalise.
Jordan will take over as House Speaker and Republican Mike Johnson declined to run again.
NPR's Barbara Sprunt says Jordan is considered a change candidate.
He's the co-founder of the ultra-conservative Freedom Caucus.
Scalise is seen as more of a moderate, an extension of that leadership era of Johnson.
And so the vote tells me that House Republicans wanted a clean break from that leadership
era.
I think folks are craving a new chapter after their massive loss last week.
NPR's Barbara Sprunt reporting.
House Democrats will choose their leadership next week.
They're widely expected to select New York Democrat Hakeem Jeffries.
He is expected to run for speaker next year when the new Congress convenes and Democrats
take power.
Meanwhile, Senate Republicans have re-elected John Thune as their leader.
House Republicans have blocked an effort to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth.
The vote was 211 to 204, and NPR's Eric McDaniel has more.
Kentucky Republican Representative Thomas Massie spearheaded this impeachment effort on his
way out of Congress.
And the charges he filed were tied to failure to get congressional approval for military
action in Iran and Yemen, as well as strikes against what the administration says are drugboats
in the Caribbean and Pacific, and a Pentagon effort to publish a Democratic senator, Markelle
of Arizona, who told service members not to follow illegal orders.
Hegseth called the charges a sham, and the White House backed him up.
Most Republicans, even those openly critical of the administration's relationship with
Congress in terms of war powers, agree the impeachment effort is now dead.
Eric McDaniel, NPR News Capitol Hill.
State officials in Pennsylvania have reported more than 1,500 measles cases so far this
year.
There are six confirmed measles-related deaths.
The greatest number of cases are in Lancaster County, home to many residents of the Amish
community.
But, as Maria Godoy reports, health officials are reaching out with a quiet vaccination
campaign.
Surveys suggest only about a third of Amish families in Lancaster County vaccinate their
children, often for cultural and practical rather than religious reasons.
But as measles spreads, health officials have been building trust by vaccinating Amish people
in their homes and hosting frequent vaccine clinics advertised solely by word of mouth.
Dr. Jennifer Wallace is with the Pennsylvania Department of Health.
They tend to be a community that does not want to have a lot of big hoopla, but also
the choice to vaccinate they consider to be a very private one.
She says the state will keep on offering these low-key vaccinations for as long as people
want them.
Maria Godoy, NPR News.
You're listening to NPR.
School officials in some European countries are reporting they're getting bomb threats
today, officials in Italy, Scotland, and Northern Ireland have rushed thousands of children
out of classrooms.
Last week, bomb threats were made against European passenger planes.
There are no reports of injuries.
In the U.S., a federal appeals court panel in Washington has ruled the Trump administration
illegally fired the director of the Voice of America.
President Trump has denounced the international broadcaster as anti-American propaganda.
His aides have slashed the VOA workforce despite orders by a federal judge to reinstate employees.
NPR's David Volkenflick has more.
Michael Abramowitz was named Voice of America's director during the Biden administration.
The veteran journalist had also served as the head of a human rights advocacy group.
Trump administration official Carrie Lake, then overseeing VOA's parent agency, forced
Abramowitz to choose between accepting a demotion to a shortwave radio facility in North Carolina
and leaving his job.
The appeals judges ruled that was illegal because Lake did not have approval from the
Senate-confirmed advisory board for VOA's parent agency, as required by law.
VOA's coverage was cut from 49 languages to just four.
Trump's nominee to head the agency has said she would build VOA back.
David Volkenflick, NPR News.
Actor Stacey Keach has died at the age of 85.
That's according to a statement from his wife.
Keach had had heart trouble.
He was famous for TV roles as well as the stage, but on TV it was for private investigator
Mike Hammer.
This is NPR.

topics.text: House Republicans elect Ohio Congressman Jim Jordan as next House Speaker, replacing Steve Scalise
House Democrats set to choose leadership next week, expected to pick Hakeem Jeffries
Senate Republicans re-elect John Thune as their leader
House Republicans block impeachment effort against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, 211 to 204
Pennsylvania reports over 1,500 measles cases this year, with quiet vaccination campaign in Amish Lancaster County
Bomb threats prompt evacuation of schools in Italy, Scotland, and Northern Ireland
Federal appeals court rules Trump administration illegally fired Voice of America director Michael Abramowitz
Actor Stacey Keach dies at age 85, known for Mike Hammer TV role
